scenario.summary: Threat actors targeted DEF CON attendees via X direct messages using a conference planning lure that directed victims to a malicious Google Doc. The document used a custom Google Apps Script sidebar to trick users into executing platform-specific malware, delivering Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) on macOS and various RAT loaders on Windows via ClickOnce and PowerShell scripts.

meta.rationale: The hunt scopes to endpoints with common browsers (Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox) which are the expected platforms for Google Doc-based lures.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using social engineering to drive users toward a malicious Google Doc sidebar that executes platform-specific scripts (macOS ClickFix or Windows ClickOnce/PowerShell loaders) from campaign infrastructure.

hunt.name: Cross-Platform Malicious Document and Script Delivery
hunt.description:
This hunt targets the initial delivery and execution phases of a post-conference phishing campaign. Attackers use X (Twitter) DMs to share a link to a Google Doc containing a custom sidebar ('DecryptPanel.html'). Depending on the visitor's OS, the sidebar delivers either a 'curl | zsh' ClickFix-style command for macOS or a ClickOnce installer (.application) and BitsTransfer-based PowerShell loader for Windows.

The hunt identifies hosts with potential exposure via browser software, stack-counts rare interactions with campaign-specific domains, and identifies behavioral patterns of remote content being interpreted directly by local shells or ClickOnce deployment engines. An agent evaluates the chain of interaction and execution to identify high-fidelity compromise events.

nodes.label: Identify hosts with potential browser exposure

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%safari%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%browser%'
config.description: Scope the hunt to hosts that have common web browsers installed, as these are the primary entry points for the Google Doc and X DM lures.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames likely used for web browsing. None means the inventory surface is empty or no common browsers are registered.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with potential browser exposure
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%safari%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%browser%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames likely used for web browsing. None means the inventory surface is empty or no common browsers are registered.

config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Identify hosts communicating with the known malicious domains using stack-counting to isolate rare phishing activity from common traffic.
config.expected_signal: Rare DNS resolutions for campaign domains. A hit indicates a host was served the lure; silence means no recent interaction with these specific domains.

primitive_config.label: Rare interactions with campaign infrastructure
primitive_config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Rare DNS resolutions for campaign domains. A hit indicates a host was served the lure; silence means no recent interaction with these specific domains.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%curl %' AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%|%zsh%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%|%sh%')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the 'ClickFix' behavioral pattern where remote content is fetched and interpreted directly by a shell, a common delivery mechanism for macOS stealer payloads.
config.expected_signal: A shell command fetching and executing a remote script. The presence of the pipe character is the primary indicator of this technique.

primitive_config.label: macOS shell-piping execution behavior

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%dfsvc.exe%' AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%.application%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%http%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the usage of the ClickOnce service (dfsvc.exe) to install applications, focusing on manifest files which are used to bypass browser warnings.
config.expected_signal: Execution of dfsvc.exe with a remote URL or .application manifest path. Many legitimate apps use this, so the agent must weigh it against the C2 domains found in other steps.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_path, script_content, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%bitstransfer%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%invoke-webrequest%') AND (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%iex%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%invoke-expression%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect PowerShell script blocks that use BitsTransfer or Invoke-WebRequest to pull and execute content, matching the loader logic described in the research.
config.expected_signal: A script block that downloads a file to %TEMP% and immediately executes it. This is a common pattern for the Sleestak/phishing loader.

config.objective: Identify hosts that resolved campaign domains ({{c2_domains}}) and subsequently executed shell scripts, ClickOnce installers, or PowerShell loaders.
config.description: Evaluate the combined evidence to determine if a host followed the phishing lure through to script or installer execution.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign based on the chain of events.
config.success_criteria: A citation-backed verdict for each host showing interaction with C2 infrastructure or execution signals.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host involving successful execution of scripts or manifests linked to campaign domains
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host involving successful execution of scripts or manifests linked to campaign domains
config.description: Route the hunt based on the triage verdict, moving to containment for clear matches.
Prevent further exfiltration or lateral movement by isolating the beachhead.
config.instructions: Isolate the host immediately. Begin evidence collection from /tmp/lksopo (macOS) or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\UpdateCache (Windows) and initiate password resets for all accounts used on the machine.

config.description: Review findings, confirm or overturn verdicts, and investigate for persistence.
config.instructions: Review the cited rows from the triage step. Check for persistence indicators such as 'com.xdivcmp.plist' on macOS. Verify if the user was targeted via social media DMs.

config.description: Summarize findings and record negative result for the campaign.
config.instructions: Record the absence of campaign-specific indicators. If DNS/HTTP interaction was found without execution, notify affected users of the phishing attempt.
